 # Pokedex - Product Specification
 
 ## Product
 
 The Pokedex application is a web application that allows users to search for and view information about Pokemon. The application will provide a user-friendly interface for browsing and searching for Pokemon, as well as detailed information about each Pokemon, including its abilities, stats, and evolutions.
 
 ## Vision
 
 The vision of the Pokedex application is to provide a comprehensive and user-friendly platform for Pokemon enthusiasts to explore and learn about their favorite Pokemon. The application will serve as a digital encyclopedia, offering detailed information and interactive features to enhance the user experience.
 
 ## Target users
 
 - Pokemon enthusiasts of all ages who want to learn more about their favorite Pokemon.
 - People who are interested in learning about different types of Pokemon and their characteristics.
 - Players of Pokemon games who want to have a reference for their in-game adventures.
 
 ## Core value
 
 The Pokedex application provides a comprehensive and user-friendly platform for Pokemon enthusiasts to explore and learn about their favorite Pokemon.
 
 ## Initial scope
 
 The first version of this application will include:
 
 - A search feature to find Pokemon by name or type.
 - A list view of Pokemon with basic information such as name, type, and image.
 - A detailed view of each Pokemon with information about its abilities, stats, and evolutions.
 - A favorites feature to save and manage favorite Pokemon.
 - A responsive design.
 - Localization (i18n) with Dutch and English in the first version.
 
 ## Technical choices
 
 - **Persistent data:** favorites are stored in SQLite so they remain available after an app restart. The alternative was AsyncStorage, but SQLite gives the saved collection a structured schema.
 - **Native feature:** the detail screen uses the React Native share sheet. The alternative was haptics, but sharing a Pokemon is more useful to this app's users and works on both mobile platforms.
 - **Server state:** TanStack Query caches PokeAPI responses and loads the list in pages of 24. The alternative was manual effects and component state, but query caching avoids duplicate requests while navigating.

 - Advanced filtering and sorting options.
 - User-generated content (e.g., reviews, ratings).
 - Social media integration.

One file per feature in `specs/features/`, for example
`specs/features/search.md`. Three to six features is enough. Every feature
becomes one GitHub issue. Delete the comments in `<>`. Half a page is plenty.

Same four headings as in Dan's lessons: Goal, Constraints, Acceptance
Criteria, Out of Scope. This is a worked example. Replace it with your own.

---

# Search a city

## Goal

<What can the user do when this is done, and why? One or two sentences.>

Find a city by typing its name, so I can see its week forecast.

## Constraints

<The walls the agent cannot see: which screen, which data, what to reuse,
what not to add.>

- Lives on the home screen, `src/app/index.tsx`. No new screen.
- Uses the Open-Meteo geocoding API (`/v1/search?name=...`). Starts from two
  letters.
- Colors and spacing from `src/constants/theme.ts`.
- No new dependencies.

## Acceptance Criteria

<Three to six things someone else can tick off without asking you anything.
What is on screen, what happens on press, what a failure looks like.>

- [ ] A search field at the top, placeholder "Search a city".
- [ ] Results show name and country while I type.
- [ ] No match shows the text "No city found".
- [ ] Tapping a result opens the week forecast for that city.
- [ ] A loading state while searching, an error with a Retry button when it fails.

## Out of Scope

<What this feature does not do. The agent will not invent it.>

- Search by postcode or coordinates.
- Search history or suggestions.
- My location (GPS).

 *   No warnings: no `console.log`, no warnings in the terminal or on screen.
 *   Offline: the app works in airplane mode with the last data it loaded.
 *   Tests: at least one test per feature on the logic (hook or service), based on its acceptance criteria. `npm test` passes.
 *   CI: a [GitHub Action](https://docs.github.com/en/actions) runs lint and tsc (and your tests) on every push.
 *   Accessibility: every button has a label for VoiceOver or TalkBack, and screens still work with the largest text size. See [accessibility](https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility).
 *   Optimistic update: saving or removing something shows at once, before the database is done, and goes back if it fails. See [optimistic updates](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/optimistic-updates).
 
 * * *
 
 ## Appendix A: Pokédex
 
 [](#appendix-a-pokédex)
 
 Follow the [Figma file](https://www.figma.com/design/dsgGXcu5WELIvRW90m5308/Pok%C3%A9mon-Code-Challenge?node-id=1-2) closely: type colours, font, spacing, icons.
 
 Every heading is one feature: one spec file, one issue.
 
 **List**
 
 *   All ~1300 Pokémon, as in the design, live from the API. Loads fast, scrolls smoothly.
 
 **Search**
 
 *   A search field as in the design. Results show while you type.
 *   Part of the name is enough, in any case: "pika" finds Pikachu.
 *   Finds every Pokémon, also one you have not scrolled to yet.
 *   Results look like the rows in the list. No match shows an empty state.
 
 PokeAPI has no search endpoint: you work out how. Look at what the API gives you before you let the agent build it.
 
 **Detail**
 
 *   Reachable from the list and from favorites.
 *   Name, number, artwork, types in the type colour.
 *   Three parts: about, stats, evolution chain. Quick to switch.
 *   Evolution chain from the API, tap through to the next detail.
 *   Favorite and unfavorite.
 
 **Favorites**
 
 *   Own screen, still there after a restart, with an empty state.
 
 **For every feature** (not a feature of its own: put these in the constraints)
 
 *   Loading and error state on list, detail and evolution chain.
 *   The font from the design with Expo Font ([fonts.zip](/Kevinvandenhoek/inholland-react-native-course/blob/main/exam/assets/fonts.zip)).
 
 **Compare (you design it)**
 
 A user puts two Pokémon side by side and sees who is stronger on which stat. Figma has no screen for this: follow its style.
 
 *   Compare any two Pokémon: per stat you see who is stronger.
 
 ## Appendix B: Battle simulator
 
 [](#appendix-b-battle-simulator)
 
 Your own design. Keep it simple: two Pokémon, HP bars, a log of the turns. Every heading is one feature: one spec file, one issue. [Impression](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/634a72c3-d79d-4452-a650-2b80561c8d43).
 
 **Setup**
 
 *   Pick two Pokémon (search or random), live from the API.
 *   Both at level 50, with their base stats from the API as they are.
 
 **The fight**
 
 *   Turns in order of speed, a tie is random.
 *   Each turn a real move of that Pokémon from the API (power, type, accuracy). Each turn the user picks the move for their own Pokémon. The opponent's move is up to you (random is fine). No move with power? The Pokémon uses [Struggle](https://pokeapi.co/api/v2/move/struggle), as in the games.
 *   Damage by the [official formula](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Damage) (generation V and later): level, attack/defense or special attack/special defense by the move's damage class, power, random 85 to 100%, STAB x1.5.
 *   Type effectiveness from the API (`/type/{id}`, `damage_relations`), not hardcoded. Both types of the defender count. Not fetched again every turn.
 *   Visible: super effective, not very effective, no effect, hit or miss.
 *   Winner when one HP reaches zero.
 
 **History**
 
 *   Every fight stored: who, who, winner, number of turns. Still there after a restart.
 *   A history screen with an empty state.
 
 **For every feature** (not a feature of its own: put these in the constraints)
 
 *   Loading and error state on search, Pokémon, moves and types.
 
 Out of scope: abilities, items, status effects, weather, special move effects (multi-hit, charging, ...), more than one Pokémon per side.
 
 * * *
 
 ## References
 
 [](#references)
 
 *   [PokeAPI docs](https://pokeapi.co/docs/v2)
 *   [Public APIs list](https://github.com/public-apis/public-apis)

 # Battle setup
 
 ## Goal
 
 Users can choose two Pokémon and start a battle using current data from
 PokeAPI. The setup is intentionally small so a user can get into a fight
 quickly.
 
 ## Constraints
 
 - The setup is reachable from the existing Pokedex navigation and opens the
   battle flow without replacing existing list, detail, or favorites flows.
 - The user chooses one Pokémon for each side by searching by name or choosing
   a random Pokémon.
 - Pokémon, base stats, moves, move details, and type-effectiveness data come
   from PokeAPI; no Pokémon or battle data is hardcoded in the app.
 - Both Pokémon start at level 50 with their base stats as returned by the API.
 - The screen must show loading and error states for every API-backed load and
   provide a retry action after an error.
 - Reuse the existing theme, localization, Expo Router navigation, and
   TanStack Query conventions. Do not add a dependency unless the existing
   project cannot provide the required behavior.
 
 ## Acceptance Criteria
 
 - [ ] **REQ-001**: A user can select one Pokémon for the player's side by
   searching by name or choosing a random Pokémon.
 - [ ] **REQ-002**: A user can select one Pokémon for the opponent's side by
   searching by name or choosing a random Pokémon.
 - [ ] **REQ-003**: The selected Pokémon's name, artwork, types, and level 50
   starting HP are visible before the battle starts.
 - [ ] **REQ-004**: The user cannot start a battle until both sides have a
   selected Pokémon.
 - [ ] **REQ-005**: Starting a valid setup opens the battle screen with both
   selected Pokémon and their API-backed battle data.
 - [ ] **REQ-006**: Loading and API failure states are visible and actionable
   for Pokémon, move, and type-effectiveness data used by setup.

 - Abilities, held items, status effects, weather, or breeding data.

 # Pokémon battle
 
 ## Goal
 
 Users can play a short turn-based battle between two level 50 Pokémon and
 understand why each turn succeeds, fails, or deals damage.
 
 ## Constraints
 
 - The battle uses one Pokémon per side and starts with the base stats returned
   by PokeAPI.
 - Turns are resolved in descending Speed order. If Speed is tied, the order is
   selected randomly once for that turn.
 - On each turn the user chooses one real move belonging to the player's
   Pokémon. The opponent's move is selected randomly from its usable moves.
 - Each move displays its API-provided power, type, and accuracy. A move without
   power uses Struggle from PokeAPI.
 - Damage follows the generation V-and-later official formula: level, the
   attack/defense pair or special-attack/special-defense pair selected by the
   move's damage class, power, a random factor from 85% through 100%, and STAB
   x1.5 when applicable.
 - Type effectiveness is read from PokeAPI's type damage relations. Both
   defender types affect the multiplier, and the type data is loaded once for
   the battle rather than fetched on every turn.
 - The battle must visibly communicate hit, miss, no effect, not very effective,
   and super effective outcomes, as well as current HP.
 - A battle ends immediately when either Pokémon reaches zero HP. The winner
   and total number of turns are then available to history.
 - The screen must show loading and error states for every API-backed load and
   provide retry or a clear way to return to setup.
 
 ## Acceptance Criteria
 
 - [ ] **REQ-007**: The battle screen shows both Pokémon, current HP, maximum
   HP, and a visible HP bar for each side.
 - [ ] **REQ-008**: The player's available moves show name, type, power, and
   accuracy, with a clear disabled or unavailable state while a turn is being
   resolved.
 - [ ] **REQ-009**: Selecting a move resolves the turn in Speed order; a Speed
   tie uses a random order for that turn.
 - [ ] **REQ-010**: A move can miss according to its accuracy, and the battle
   log explicitly reports the miss without reducing HP.
 - [ ] **REQ-011**: A successful move calculates damage using level 50, the
   correct physical or special stat pair, move power, the 85–100% random factor,
   and STAB when the attacker shares the move type.
 - [ ] **REQ-012**: Damage applies type effectiveness for both defender types
   using API-provided relations, and the log identifies no effect, not very
   effective, super effective, or a normal hit.
 - [ ] **REQ-013**: When a Pokémon reaches zero HP, the battle stops accepting
   moves and identifies the winner.
 - [ ] **REQ-014**: Every resolved turn adds a readable entry to a battle log
   containing the actor, move, outcome, and damage or miss result.
 - [ ] **REQ-015**: Loading and API failure states are visible for Pokémon,
   moves, and type-effectiveness data, with retry behavior that does not create
   duplicate turns.
 
 ## Out of Scope
 
 - Abilities, held items, critical hits, status effects, weather, recoil,
   priority, switching, multi-hit moves, charging moves, and other special move
   effects.
 - Experience, leveling, evolution, capture, or team management.
 - Player-versus-player networking or an opponent controlled by an account.

   empty state.

 - Editing, sharing, exporting, or deleting individual history entries.

`expo-sqlite` gives your app access to a database that can be queried through a SQLite API. The database is persisted across restarts of your app.

> On Apple TV, the underlying database file is in the caches directory and not the application documents directory, per [Apple platform guidelines](https://github.com/react-native-tvos/react-native-tvos/issues/68#issuecomment-628327676).

## Installation

#### Install library

```sh
# npm
npx expo install expo-sqlite

# yarn
yarn expo install expo-sqlite

# pnpm
pnpm expo install expo-sqlite

# bun
bun expo install expo-sqlite
```

If you are installing this in an [existing React Native app](https://docs.expo.dev/bare/overview.md), make sure to [install `expo`](https://docs.expo.dev/bare/installing-expo-modules.md) in your project.

#### Start with an example

The [`with-sqlite`](https://github.com/expo/examples/tree/master/with-sqlite) example comes with `expo-sqlite` already installed and configured:

```sh
# npm
npx create-expo-app --example with-sqlite

# yarn
yarn create expo-app --example with-sqlite

# pnpm
pnpm create expo-app --example with-sqlite

# bun
bun create expo --example with-sqlite
```


 # Pokémon battle
 
 ## Goal
 
 Users can play a short turn-based battle between two level 50 Pokémon and
 understand why each turn succeeds, fails, or deals damage.
 
 ## Constraints
 
 - The battle uses one Pokémon per side and starts with the base stats returned
   by PokeAPI.
 - Turns are resolved in descending Speed order. If Speed is tied, the order is
   selected randomly once for that turn.
 - On each turn the user chooses one real move belonging to the player's
   Pokémon. The opponent's move is selected randomly from its usable moves.
 - Each move displays its API-provided power, type, and accuracy. A move without
   power uses Struggle from PokeAPI.
 - Damage follows the generation V-and-later official formula: level, the
   attack/defense pair or special-attack/special-defense pair selected by the
   move's damage class, power, a random factor from 85% through 100%, and STAB
   x1.5 when applicable.
 - Type effectiveness is read from PokeAPI's type damage relations. Both
   defender types affect the multiplier, and the type data is loaded once for
   the battle rather than fetched on every turn.
 - The battle must visibly communicate hit, miss, no effect, not very effective,
   and super effective outcomes, as well as current HP.
 - A battle ends immediately when either Pokémon reaches zero HP. The winner
   and total number of turns are then available to history.
 - The screen must show loading and error states for every API-backed load and
   provide retry or a clear way to return to setup.
 
 ## Acceptance Criteria
 
 - [ ] **REQ-007**: The battle screen shows both Pokémon, current HP, maximum
   HP, and a visible HP bar for each side.
 - [ ] **REQ-008**: The player's available moves show name, type, power, and
   accuracy, with a clear disabled or unavailable state while a turn is being
   resolved.
 - [ ] **REQ-009**: Selecting a move resolves the turn in Speed order; a Speed
   tie uses a random order for that turn.
 - [ ] **REQ-010**: A move can miss according to its accuracy, and the battle
   log explicitly reports the miss without reducing HP.
 - [ ] **REQ-011**: A successful move calculates damage using level 50, the
   correct physical or special stat pair, move power, the 85–100% random factor,
   and STAB when the attacker shares the move type.
 - [ ] **REQ-012**: Damage applies type effectiveness for both defender types
   using API-provided relations, and the log identifies no effect, not very
   effective, super effective, or a normal hit.
 - [ ] **REQ-013**: When a Pokémon reaches zero HP, the battle stops accepting
   moves and identifies the winner.
 - [ ] **REQ-014**: Every resolved turn adds a readable entry to a battle log
   containing the actor, move, outcome, and damage or miss result.
 - [ ] **REQ-015**: Loading and API failure states are visible for Pokémon,
   moves, and type-effectiveness data, with retry behavior that does not create
   duplicate turns.
 
 ## Out of Scope
 
 - Abilities, held items, critical hits, status effects, weather, recoil,
   priority, switching, multi-hit moves, charging moves, and other special move
   effects.
 - Experience, leveling, evolution, capture, or team management.
 - Player-versus-player networking or an opponent controlled by an account.

 ## Goal
 
 Users can review completed battles after leaving the battle and after
 restarting the app, so the battle feature has a persistent result beyond the

 - Save only completed battles after a winner has been determined.
 - Store enough information to display both Pokémon, the winner, and the number

   from favorites.

   empty state.

 ## Acceptance Criteria
 
 - [ ] **REQ-016**: A completed battle is stored with the player's Pokémon,
   opponent's Pokémon, winner, and total number of turns.
